text:
Maria K: quick thought for rollout privacy/UX: what if we stop exposing raw pins/hashes in X-Model-Version and instead return an opaque 'serving token' + semantic tags?
Sam H: by 'serving token' do you mean a stable id per variant that clients can log but can't reverse?
Maria K: exactly. e.g. header: `X-Model-Version: token=svc-7f2a;tier=stable;cohort=42` and a separate `X-Model-Features: kvcache=true,quant=8bit`
Lee C: how would we debug an incident if everything is opaque? ops need to map token -> full metadata quickly.
Maria K: internal mapping service holds token -> {variant_id, fingerprint, publish_time}. Traces get internal-only fields `internal.model.fingerprint` (scrubbed from outward traces).
Ada P: some enterprise customers currently rely on fingerprint for reproducibility. Masking might break their workflows. Can we gate raw visibility?
Mason R: propose: default masked for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private provide tenant-configurable `expose_raw_version` toggle which enables `X-Model-Version-Raw` in responses for that tenant.
Sam H: good compromise. We should also version the header format and update SDKs to avoid brittle parsing.
Maria K: rollout steps I suggest: (1) publish new masked header format behind feature flag, (2) add tenant opt-in for raw header, (3) update SDKs and docs, (4) enable by default after 45 days.
Lee C: telemetry note: never use fingerprint or full hash as metric labels. Use a low-cardinality derived label like `serving_variant_token` that maps to token. If mapping absent return `unknown_token` and increment `variant.token_miss` metric.
Ada P: plus add audit that tokens cannot be deterministic embeddings of tenant or PII. Use HMAC(service_key, variant_id || salt) truncated to 12 chars.
Mason R: infra work: need token mapping store with TTL and on-disk snapshot for backfilling traces. Also a backfill job to annotate historical spans when we flip on masking. I can own that.
Sam H: schema question: should we add token into the rollout manifest as `token_hint` or compute tokens when publishing?
Maria K: compute at publish-time; keep manifest lean (variants: id, fingerprint, rules). Token generation is a sidecar concern so we can rotate keys without changing manifests.
Lee C: lifecycle: when a canary is promoted, token stability matters. If variant identity persists, keep token; if fingerprint changes, emit `token_rotated` event in telemetry.
Ada P: regulatory checklist: if a tenant requests full raw header we should log consent in audit logs and limit retention.
Infra Bot: feature-flag `features.masked_version_header` added to rollout-service; gating checks pass for canary infra.
Sam H: someone volunteer to draft a short RFC with header examples, SDK compatibility guidance, metrics semantics, and opt-in flow?
Maria K: I'll draft the RFC and include an ops playbook snippet for handling `unknown_token` cases.
Mason R: I'll prepare the backfill job spec and infra changes (mapping store + snapshots).
Lee C: add a tiny ops snippet in RFC: ```
# ops flow: token==unknown spike
1) check `variant.token_miss` alerting rules
2) query token-mapping-store for time window of traces
3) if missing, run backfill for affected time range and annotate traces
```
Sam H: cool. let's review RFC in next architecture sync. :thumbsup:
